hypothesis: Source identity cues can let a document-reader answer service-purpose questions correctly despite incorrect role text. Opaque anchors should reduce this false acceptance without losing supported content localization.
scope: Evaluation mechanism for OS descriptions, not a claim of improved writer or whole-prose correctness.
development: 22 maintainer-authored ThreadX service purpose lines with independently located source definitions
references: Official rtos-docs version 1e36a62618de3771c973196e7648cba50d19cf1f and portable ThreadX core 06dabb0ad0403f59889ce85eeb3d48dbd9d3759b. Service identities and Ctags spans, not an LLM judgment.
controls: Wrong roles are a deterministic derangement of the same source anchors and purpose text. Positive role text comes unchanged from maintainers. Masking changes only identity cues, not source semantics or claim content.
gate: Positive masked exact localization >=90% in both repeats; wrong-role score must fall by >=50 percentage points after masking in both repeats. This only passes artifact-sensitivity pilot, not overall method suitability or novelty.
strong_simple_baseline: Deterministic token-overlap role-text search, which sees the identical sanitized documents and questions; if it matches the masked reader controls, retain masking only as an evaluation diagnostic, not a new research method.
failures: API failure, malformed output, unknown, wrong, budget exhaustion separately retained; unchanged question denominator 22; no format retry or post-hoc threshold change
stop: No prompts or samples tuned after results. If simple baseline already solves controls, retire this standalone research candidate. Any later use must be as diagnostics of a genuinely different generator experiment.
limits: Original manual purpose lines can be stale or underspecified, so this is source-identity/role-localization truth, not verified kernel behavior
This does not establish judge understanding speed
No production-model quality claim, no held-out confirmation if development gate or strong-baseline requirement fails
QA metrics and name obfuscation are existing research; this combination is not assumed novel
